summary: Driving y yielded promises requires observing and returning every one of their outcomes, and the controller performs constant overhead per yield with one live bridge.

optimality.argument: For a normally completing generator with y yields, every yielded promise can affect later generator state and the final return, so the controller must process all y outcomes. The accepted driver performs one promise bridge and one next-or-throw transition per yield, matching the Omega(y) lower bound.

replacement_checks.evidence: Any one of the y yielded outcomes may change the generator's next state or final return value, so none can be skipped in a complete execution.
Each yield creates one temporary bridge and causes one generator next or throw call, for O(y) overhead and constant live controller state.
Regression executes immediate and delayed completion, resolved and rejected yields, caught and uncaught cancellation, next-yield recovery, and cancellation after completion.
